newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Lend Lease profit disappoints market.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Lend Lease profit disappoints market.

text.p: Ambitious property and financial services company Lend Lease Corp Ltd on Friday became one of the few Australian bluechips to achieve higher profits in the current annual reporting season and forecast even better times as costs are cut at home and overseas projects near completion.

Brokers and analysts, however, were less than impressed by the 7.6 percent rise in 1995/96 net profit to A$280.0 million and instead fussed about how the company achieved its growth in the year just gone. "In our view it was a bit of a disappointing number," said the head trader of a European-owned broking house.
"We were going for a slightly higher profit, especially as the tax rate was so low," he said, referring to a more than threefold cut in the tax bill to A$9.6 million.
Shares in Lend Lease tracked the rest of the sharemarket lower on Friday, with the stock eight cents weaker at A$20.90 at 1.30 p.m. (0330 gmt) but 20 cents off its day's low.

The result was near the middle of expectations which ranged from a low of A$273 million to a high of A$290 million, with analysts correctly forecasting that profits would again be dominated by the MLC funds and insurance group, as well as dividends from its investment in Westpac Banking Corp.

Financial services increased net profit by 39 percent to A$211.4 million, including a A$12 million rise in dividend payments from Westpac to A$52 million and a once-off gain of A$26 million from the Australian Eagle life insurance unit due to accounting changes. Lend Lease has a direct stake in the major Australian bank of three percent after selling a six percent holding via a warrant issue earlier in the year.

The property section achieved a net profit of A$40.2 million against A$92.4 million a year earlier, but the latest year included an unexpected one-time writedown of A$57 million on the value of two shopping centres in Victoria.
Managing director David Higgins said the 1995/96 profit result was a strong one, especially as it included an unexpected after tax provision of A$57 million from property revaluations.

"Lend Lease has delivered a profit of A$280 million in an Australian environment of low growth and low inflation and that is despite a once-off provision for two shopping centres in Victoria," Higgins said at a news conference.

He said net profit would rise further in 1996/97, but would not be more specific. By the year 2000, however, Higgins said he expected to have achieved double digit rises in sales and net profits from the financial services division.
Higgins said the company would decide in the next month or so on further property investments in Jakarta, Bangkok, and the United Kingdom.

Lend Lease is the driving force behind the A$1.2 billion Bluewater Shopping Centre in Kent which is due to open in 1999 and this year announced plans to extend its European retail development business with the acquisition of 50 percent of U.K.-based Chelverton Properties Ltd.

Asian property developments achieved a sharp rise in 1995/96 net profit to A$28.5 million from A$3.7 million, with Higgins saying this confirmed Lend Lease's intended transition from a domestic to an international company.

Higgins said he could not make a specific prediction on the profit increase expected from the property division, which includes project management and development in Australia, Asia, the United Kingdom, and the United States.
"We will be making more investments in the next few months in Asia and the UK. We will be deploying our capital where we find the right opportunities," he said.

Higgins said the improvment in the financial services division would be driven by a reduction of up to 40 percent in operating costs and the continued introduction of simplified, and profitable, insurance and investment products.
"This is not an extraordinary result in any way," the analyst said. "But given that companies like Boral are down 30 percent maybe a flat profit is very acceptable."
